description: #919 golden vertical: what hardware to buy + where it applies + what operation to fabricate, computed INDEPENDENTLY by hand and matched exactly by the engine. The contact scenario uses identity bases so every number is derivable on paper (the arithmetic is documented per section). Demand and BOM sections carry the #917/#875 domain math. NO number in this file was generated by the resolver; a mismatch is a finding, never a regeneration.

contactScenario.comment: Shelf end (participant A, role A rules) glued onto the side's inner face (participant B, role B rules). Identity bases; A's local X spans the 100mm contact edge, A's local Z is the shelf's thickness direction (bottom face = local Z=0), B's basis maps its local Y to assembly -Z so its back face (local Y=0) is coplanar with A's bottom (assembly Z=0).

frame.comment: origin = overlap start along A.X, centered on the cross overlap: (0, 9, 0); axis = A.X = (1,0,0); normal = A's bottom outward = (0,0,-1).

stations.comment: count=2, margins 30/30 over the [0,100] overlap: distance = 0+30 + i*(100-30-30)/(2-1) -> 30 and 70 (the last station is pinned to `last`).

rules.comment: Housing on the SHELF (participant A): enters the bottom face (local Z=0), drills assembly +Z (rule axis (0,-1,0) projects through the contact normal (0,0,-1) to (0,0,+1)), depth 13 leaves 5mm. Offset zero: the center sits exactly on the station.
Dowel on the SIDE (participant B): enters B's back face (local Y=0 = the contact plane), drills local +Y (assembly -Z) into the 18mm side, depth 12 leaves 6mm.

expectedOperations.comment: Rules x stations, hosted by participant role. Hand arithmetic: rule axes are ASSEMBLY directions projected through (along, normal, cross): cam (0,-1,0) -> (0,0,+1) -> shelf-local (0,0,1); dowel (0,1,0) -> (0,0,-1) = B.Basis.Y -> side-local (0,+1,0). Cam centers = station points in A-local (identity): (30,9,0) and (70,9,0). Dowel centers = stations in B-local: (30,0,9) and (70,0,9).

mutations.comment: Isolation arithmetic, each applied to the base scenario independently.

cases.name: margin moves only the affected stations
station count 3 redistributes the pattern
cases.comment: distance = 30 + i*40/2 over [30,70] -> 30, 50, 70; hole count per rule 3.

cases.name: recipe revision bump changes provenance and the technical fingerprint inputs, never geometry
technical profile revision bump changes provenance and the fingerprint input; operation identity stays recipe-scoped
cases.comment: Pinned contract: the per-operation OperationID is RECIPE-scoped (a profile revision bump keeps it stable), while the machining fingerprint input carries technicalProfileId/Revision — so the technical fingerprint still moves. Folding the profile revision into the OperationID would be an industrial identity contract change and needs explicit owner authorization; it is deliberately NOT done here.

failClosed.comment: The same scenario without a verified technical profile must stay no-fabricable: the derivation returns TECHNICAL_PROFILE_REQUIRED and zero operations.

demandScenario.comment: #917: demand = profile items x VERIFIED contacts (station-independent). One profile, two items, two contacts -> each hardware consumes item quantity x 2.

bomScenario.comment: Representative cabinet board list (#919) with formula-derived dims at 600x720x560, T=18 (back 15 thick, 15 inset). Hardware unit prices come from the Hardware rows; requirements quantity = consumed units (no package rounding in this scenario).

expectedHardwareDemand.comment: 2 contacts x items (1 minifix + 2 dowels) — same arithmetic as demandScenario.
